slides.title: The System Today: One FGO, Joint Fault Handling, Rolling Integrity
slides.question: How are estimation, fault exclusion and protection connected in the live UWB–IMU system?
slides.takeaway: A coupled incremental estimator and rolling fault-aware position integrity layer goes beyond a per-epoch UWB RAIM test.
slides.caption: Raw measurements drive one incremental FGO and parallel fault monitors; the selector commits at most one native update. A rolling certificate carries state uncertainty, fault consequences and source/risk identity across marginalization.
speaker_notes: Follow the single estimator path and the two fault-monitor inputs into the hypothesis pool.
Proof proposal precedes commit; final HPL/VPL are bound to the actual commit receipt and tag center.
The boundary carries position, velocity, rotation, biases, historical faults and shared source/risk identity.
The risk horizon is not the 30-epoch explicit window; no second FGO or all-history resolve is required.

slides.title: E00 — What Was Actually Tested, and Which Comparisons Are Valid?
slides.question: Which datasets, ground truths and algorithm modes support a defensible comparison?
slides.takeaway: Comparability comes before APE rankings: Walk reference and STAR input contracts remain open.
slides.caption: Rows identify pre-registered real recordings, rather than six successful examples. The producer-to-estimator lanes keep conditional simulation integrity separate from empirical real data and overlays.
speaker_notes: SUCCESS is a process exit status, not proof of complete input or output coverage.
Simulation is the only registered source with conditional raw qualification.
Real recordings use O-FDE-ENG / O-ENG-NOFDE; semi-synthetic labels concern the added fault only.
Own-Vicon calibration uses a disclosed segmented TEST-involved fit; SFUISE official rejection remains enabled.

slides.title: E01 — Healthy Simulation: Good Accuracy Under the Declared Model
slides.question: How accurately does the coupled pipeline localize without imposed faults?
slides.takeaway: The healthy pipeline delivers approximately 5 cm tag RMSE in the registered simulated model.
slides.caption: Each point is one independent seed; lower world-frame tag APE is better, without trajectory alignment. SFUISE uses sensor-only initialization, while ours receives an independently noisy initial observation: this is not an optimizer-only comparison.
speaker_notes: All three fixed healthy seeds are shown, without seed selection or fitted alignment.
FULL and NOFDE coincide on the healthy source; SFUISE online and final are distinct views.
Final history excludes the support-invalid bootstrap prefix; it is neither causal nor a full batch optimum.
The approximate five-centimeter result is conditional on the registered simulation and initialization information.

slides.title: E02 — Real-Data Validation Is Currently an Interface Problem
slides.question: Which real-data comparisons can we physically interpret?
slides.takeaway: Apparent algorithm failures cannot yet be separated from missing physical frame and timing validation.
slides.caption: Traces show the frozen own-Vicon TEST output and height reference, with its GT-assisted calibration disclosed. The matrix separates physically unresolved Walk references and STAR input conventions from conditional empirical scoring.
speaker_notes: Use R3 as an empirical example, not an independently calibrated blind test.
Its registered TEST begins at 16.678774643 seconds; FULL has no complete TEST trajectory.
Walk physical APE, ARE and RPE are unavailable despite saved numerical proxy distances.
STAR kilometer-scale divergence is retained in the frozen report, but the gyro input contract prevents intrinsic method ranking.

slides.title: E02 — Real FDE Execution, Not Nominal Localization, Is the Bottleneck
slides.question: Can the fault-handling pipeline sustain a complete real recording?
slides.takeaway: The main real-data blocker is FDE execution continuity, beyond nominal FGO data loading.
slides.caption: Bars show coverage of the registered GT TEST grid, with interpolation limited to 100 ms; NA is not zero. This measures emitted-output continuity, not accuracy or raw integrity, and Walk coverage is temporal only.
speaker_notes: The denominator is each original GT TEST grid within IMU source bounds, not successful matches or commit attempts.
Walk percentages describe time coverage only; the physical reference is unresolved.
The R3 FULL TEST coverage is unavailable and must not be drawn as a zero bar.
Four of six engineering FULL runs hit the registered resource stop; all real raw PL remains unqualified.

slides.title: E03 — FDE Benefits Are Fault-Dependent, Not Uniformly Positive
slides.question: Does FDE actually improve position and attitude accuracy?
slides.takeaway: Accel/joint positioning improves, but gyro-only accuracy and state recovery remain unresolved.
slides.caption: Each point is a matched seed; positive OFF−ON means FDE reduced RMSE, while negative values show degradation. Position improvement cannot cancel worsening body attitude, particularly under accel or gyro faults.
speaker_notes: Three independently registered seeds per fault class supply the matched ON/OFF gains.
UWB-only is not uniformly positive; accelerometer positioning gains accompany worse attitude.
Gyro-only has a large negative seed and negative mean position and attitude gains.
Joint-fault mean attitude gain hides per-seed variation; no significance claim is made from three seeds.

slides.title: E03 — Real Isolation Can Still Be Followed by Estimation Drift
slides.question: What happens before, during and after a detected joint fault?
slides.takeaway: Post-FDE state consistency and recovery determine net accuracy; isolation alone is insufficient.
slides.caption: Bands mark source-level injections and receipt rows mark actual detection, isolation, prior repair and rejoined state. The APE axis is linear below 0.1 m and logarithmic above; a successful transaction does not certify state-error recovery.
speaker_notes: The title uses real isolation to mean actual native transactions; this example is T-SIM, not a real recording.
The exact stream is SC8-J, seed 20261020, 600 epochs.
The raw accel pulse is 20 m/s² for 500 ms and UWB bias is 2.25 m for three epochs.
Rejoined is a persistent state flag; episode success requires actual prior replacement, bridge and consecutive post-bridge rejoined commits.

slides.title: E04 — Horizontal Stanford: Conservative Bounds, Conditional Coverage
slides.question: How do horizontal position errors relate to the emitted HPL?
slides.takeaway: Horizontal bounds cover the registered errors but remain much wider than the observed error.
slides.caption: HPE is horizontal and HPL vertical; darker teal log-count bins have more timely samples, and points above dashed y=x are empirically covered. Gray bins are late (excluded from timely availability); dotted lines mark research ALs (2/5/10 m), and zero correlated violations do not establish empirical 10^-6 risk.
speaker_notes: The Stanford panels use actual histogram counts for the registered E01/E03 main cases.
Overall qualified receipt total includes other experiments and must not be confused with this figure denominator.
An HPL above HPE is coverage, whereas an HPL above HAL is unavailable at that alert limit.
The conditional theorem comes from the declared source event, not independence of these correlated observations.

slides.title: E04 — Vertical Stanford: Availability Depends on the Application AL
slides.question: Why can a centimeter-level estimate still be unavailable?
slides.takeaway: PL tightness and application availability are distinct from estimator accuracy, especially vertically.
slides.caption: VPE is horizontal and VPL vertical; darker teal bins contain more timely samples, gray bins are late, and bins above dashed y=x have VPL≥VPE. Dotted research ALs (3/5/10 m) test admissibility; the healthy AL comparison changes evaluation only, not estimates or PL, and is not certification.
speaker_notes: Vertical bounds can exceed the chosen VAL even when VPE is small.
Healthy joint availability divides timely H/V-admissible receipts by all 600 planned epochs per seed.
Research 2/3 and 5/5 meter ALs are post-processing diagnostics and do not alter solver parameters.
No hardware safety requirement or real-data protection qualification is inferred.

slides.title: E05 — 30 vs 1000 Epochs: When Is a Longer Window Worth It?
slides.question: Does retaining much more history improve accuracy or integrity enough to justify the cost?
slides.takeaway: Keep 30/30 as the online reference; extend history only when measured recovery benefits justify cost.
slides.caption: APE uses the same complete 1,000-epoch scoring interval; bubble area denotes sampled RSS, not process peak. LF, LI and recovery replay vary together in the coupled sweep, so its fault benefit cannot be attributed to PL alone.
speaker_notes: Every plotted configuration ran 2100 epochs and the common scoring interval is 1101 through 2100.
Coupled LF=LI uses 30, 100, 300, 600 and 1000 actual UWB epochs; 1000 is 50 seconds.
The fixed LF=300 sweep uses LI=30, 100 and 300, reusing the shared 300/300 result.
The resource marker is a sampled RSS maximum, not the unknown between-sample peak; larger windows are intentionally allowed to miss real-time targets.

slides.title: E06 — Runtime Breakdown: Fast Simulation, Expensive Real FDE
slides.question: Where does the computation go, and which timing numbers are comparable?
slides.takeaway: The small-window simulated full path meets study P95 targets; current real engineering FDE does not.
slides.caption: Curves show measured whole-service latency; solid is core and dashed is sink, while stacked bars contain additive exclusive means. Stage P95s are not additive, and SFUISE buffering/software-clock timing represents different capabilities.
speaker_notes: Core and sink nearest-rank P95 targets remain 40 and 50 milliseconds; timely spatial fraction must also exceed 95 percent.
The healthy seed20 main E01 profile and the E06 joint repeat have distinct run IDs.
The nominal-only two-millisecond path lacks the full integrity capability and is not a like-for-like speed claim.
All measurable slow and abort frames remain; censored suffixes have no imputed timing and no complete-stream throughput claim.

slides.title: E07 — Ablations: Which Integrity Components Actually Matter?
slides.question: Are rolling constraints and recovery logic causally necessary, or just complexity?
slides.takeaway: Set constraints and geometry-aware numerical recovery have measurable effects; failures remain visible.
slides.caption: Cells show actual values and signed changes from matched FULL; red means increase and blue means decrease. G2 has no qualified output, so APE/PL are NA; the joint/sample0 switch also removes support and cannot isolate both effects.
speaker_notes: M means same committed center, A means full trajectory comparison and P means performance.
Disabling terminal support reverts to a valid conservative box.
The joint/sample0 ablation is a combined joint-plus-support reversion, not two independently isolated effects.
G2 disables dedicated numerical recovery and commits zero of eighty epochs; its measured abort cost is retained in the report.

slides.title: E08 — Long-Run Integrity: Healthy Complete, Repeated-Fault Case Censored
slides.question: Does the full pipeline sustain 10,000 epochs and process the last injected fault?
slides.takeaway: Continuous recovery at scale is unproven: FULL stops where the no-FDE route continues.
slides.caption: Curves stop at actual committed output; a blank FULL suffix is unprocessed data, not zero error. Vertical marks are scheduled faults, and the final episode beyond epoch 7171 was not verified by FULL.
speaker_notes: Process SUCCESS does not imply the ten-thousand-epoch FULL plan completed.
The producer released the full schedule but queue delivery and actual commits ended early for FULL.
NOFDE continues to the final scheduled episode, but it implements a different fault-handling policy.
Slots grow with time despite a bounded active state window; there is no constant-memory or perpetual full-state observability claim.

slides.title: Synthesis — What We Have Demonstrated, and What Remains Open
slides.question: Which claims can we defend in a paper today?
slides.takeaway: The strongest current contribution is conditional rolling fault-aware position integrity; real execution remains open.
slides.caption: Each row pairs a defensible claim with direct evidence and its limiting assumptions. Mathematical containment, empirical error, execution continuity and application certification answer different questions.
speaker_notes: The 77131 receipts span correlated scenarios and windows, rather than independent risk trials.
State estimation, integrity validity, deadline passage and application availability are distinct results.
Real calibration, engineering execution, historical export support and missing SFUISE state metrics remain explicit gaps.
Weak-UWB amplitude and S1/S2 bias studies were not registered and are not filled with older SC7 data.

slides.title: Questions for the Advisor — Decisions Needed Before the Next Study
slides.question: Which scope, resources and priorities should guide the next study?
slides.takeaway: Requested outcome: agree on the paper scope, calibration resource owner and research priority order.
slides.caption: The four questions request concrete decisions on scope, calibration resources, recovery priorities and application requirements. The next protocol should follow those decisions before a limited, newly frozen rerun.
speaker_notes: Ask for a near-term publication scope rather than an abstract endorsement.
Identify an owner for independent extrinsics, clocks and held-out calibration data.
Choose whether state-recovery research or bounded engineering execution comes first.
Agree on application HAL, VAL, TTA, covered faults and failure action before the next protocol.
